messages.subject: multivariate logistic model

messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] multivariate logistic model
parts:
Hi Paul,

Sure, here it is (also the code to simulate the data)

library(MASS)
library(brms)
sigma1 <- 1.5
sigma2 <- 0.5
rho12 <- 0.75
cov12 <- rho12*sqrt(0.5)*sqrt(1.5)
Sigma <- matrix(c(sigma1, cov12, cov12, sigma2), 2, 2)
Sigma
b0 <- -2
exp(b0)/(1 + exp(b0))
N <- 100
e.vill <- mvrnorm(n = N, rep(0, 2), Sigma)
p <- exp(b0 + e.vill)/(1 + exp(b0 + e.vill))
examined <- sample(seq(50:300), size = N, replace = T)
y1 <- rbinom(n = N, size = examined, prob = p[,1])
y2 <- rbinom(n = N, size = examined, prob = p[,2])
dat <- data.frame(y1, y2, n1 = examined, n2 = examined)

y1_f <- bf(y1 | trials(n1) ~ 0 + intercept)
y2_f <- bf(y2 | trials(n2) ~ 0 + intercept)
f <- mvbf(y1_f, y2_f)

fit <- brm(
  formula = f,
  family = binomial, 
  data = dat, chains = 4, cores = 4, seed = 194838
)

messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] multivariate logistic model
parts:
1.

brms cannot yet handle missing values on the fly, but it is on my ToDo list (see https://github.com/paul-buerkner/brms/issues/27).
What you can do is fitting multiple imputed data sets via brm_multiple (currently github version only)

2. This is possible. Simply write for instance

y1_f <- bf(y1 | trials(n1) ~ (1 | p | group))
y2_f <- bf(y2 | trials(n2) ~ (1 | p | group))

I call this "ID-syntax". The symbol "p" is arbitrary. You can also use something else. See also ?bf and vignette("brms_multilevel")

Sure, here it is (also the code to simulate the data)

library(MASS)
library(brms)
sigma1 <- 1.5
sigma2 <- 0.5
rho12 <- 0.75
cov12 <- rho12*sqrt(0.5)*sqrt(1.5)
Sigma <- matrix(c(sigma1, cov12, cov12, sigma2), 2, 2)
Sigma
b0 <- -2
exp(b0)/(1 + exp(b0))
N <- 100
e.vill <- mvrnorm(n = N, rep(0, 2), Sigma)
p <- exp(b0 + e.vill)/(1 + exp(b0 + e.vill))
examined <- sample(seq(50:300), size = N, replace = T)
y1 <- rbinom(n = N, size = examined, prob = p[,1])
y2 <- rbinom(n = N, size = examined, prob = p[,2])
dat <- data.frame(y1, y2, n1 = examined, n2 = examined)

y1_f <- bf(y1 | trials(n1) ~ 0 + intercept)
y2_f <- bf(y2 | trials(n2) ~ 0 + intercept)
f <- mvbf(y1_f, y2_f)

fit <- brm(
  formula = f,
  family = binomial, 
  data = dat, chains = 4, cores = 4, seed = 194838
)

On Thursday, 18 January 2018 10:10:24 UTC, Paul Buerkner wrote:
1.

brms cannot yet handle missing values on the fly, but it is on my ToDo list (see https://github.com/paul-buerkner/brms/issues/27).
What you can do is fitting multiple imputed data sets via brm_multiple (currently github version only)

2. This is possible. Simply write for instance

y1_f <- bf(y1 | trials(n1) ~ (1 | p | group))
y2_f <- bf(y2 | trials(n2) ~ (1 | p | group))

I call this "ID-syntax". The symbol "p" is arbitrary. You can also use something else. See also ?bf and vignette("brms_multilevel")
